current_example.problem: Find the set of values of $x$ that satisfy $6x-1 \leq 2$ or $5x-1 > 9.$ Express your answer in interval notation.
current_example.worked_solution:
We start by solving $6x-1 \leq 2\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}6x-1 & \le 2 \\ 6x & \le 3 \\ x & \le \frac{3}{6} \\ x & \le \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196049/assets/dd2c101e02e14a147371bc1b822f3bc86081dd0059ac50ae1f9131909e73e3ad.png)

Then, we solve $5x -1 > 9\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}5x-1 & >9 \\ 5x & >10 \\ x & >2\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196049/assets/8b252e1c42dcac87072a33b33460a887b6ec3bfa0d1511f05a004935df1911ca.png)

To graph the values of $x$ that satisfy either inequality, we overlay the two graphs on the same number line:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196049/assets/ac44f335b135463820ec0db9bc04470769fee7aabc8717edcc351893b6d8de47.png)

Therefore, the final solution is $x \leq \dfrac{1}{2}$ or $x >2.$ We can write this using interval notation as

$$
\begin{aligned}(-\infty ,\frac{1}{2}]\cup (2,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
